description: This class is designed for EMT's to review their knowledge of pre-hospital emergency care and practice pre-hospital emergency skills not frequently performed. Verifying skill proficiency and continuing medical education units to apply for State recertification may be achieved with attendance to lectures and practical labs. The new State recertification practical exam may be taken at an additional cost.

This class prepares students to become knowledgeable and effective pre-hospital emergency care providers. You will be trained in airway and breathing management beyond BLS guidelines, automatic defibrillation of patients in cardiac arrest, recognizing and treating shock, bleeding control and bandaging, fracture management and splinting, spinal immobilization, and proper handling of patients. Upon successful completion of the course, you will be eligible for state and national EMT certification.

This innovative camp introduces students to the fun and practical side of artificial intelligence while teaching them how to use it responsibly. Campers will explore creative projects like generating story ideas, designing art, making games, and even creating mythical lands and creatures. They'll learn how AI can help with grammar checks, homework support, and brainstorming - but also why critical thinking and ethical use matter. From making crossword puzzles and trivia games to turning pets into characters and designing comics, this camp blends imagination with tech skills for a truly unique experience.

This camp introduces students to the fascinating world of artificial intelligence and machine learning. Throughout the week, students will explore how computers recognize patterns, process images, and make decisions similar to real AI systems. They will experiment with creating simple machine-learning models and train them using sounds, images, or movements. Students will observe how their models improve and adapt as new information is introduced, simulating the behavior of a digital brain. To apply their learning, students will integrate AI concepts into creative projects, games, Scratch programming, and interactive designs. All materials and devices will be provided for use in class. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

Students will get creative in this introductory digital art class. Digital art is the new future for modern illustrations, concept art, comic art, and more. In this class, students will learn to digitally draw and paint using Adobe Creative Suite. They will pick up tricks, tips, and shortcuts to make their digital art come to life. Plus, with their own Wacom tablet or iPad, students can keep practicing their skills at home.

Students will continue advancing their understanding of digital paint mediums in this advanced digital art course. They will learn more in-depth techniques and tricks to use in digital illustrations. Digital design techniques will also be taught for those aspiring to become future concept artists, environment painters, and character designers. Students should come prepared with their preferred digital drawing gear they may already own.

Leaving behind the traditional world of pen and paper, students will learn all the ins and outs of creating paintings digitally. This course combines instruction on foundational painting/drawing skills + snazzy digital techniques so that students can make their ideas a reality. Students are required to bring their own digital drawing tools (either a laptop with a drawing tablet & photoshop, or an iPad with Procreate). Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

It is time for students to bring their video game character to life. They will discover how personality should affect every inch of a character's movement, from weight to mood. After storyboarding their animation on paper, students will jump into Maya software and learn the techniques required to make animations feel as real as possible. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students will take the next step in their game-making journey and start creating games from the ground up. Using the powerful Unreal Engine and guided by Utah Games graduates, they will develop the skills needed to become level designers and gameplay programmers. Students will combine everything they have learned, from coding to design, to build a final prototype in this in-depth, hands-on game development workshop. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Take the next step in your game making career and start creating games from the ground up. Using the powerful Unreal Engine and taught by Utah Games graduates, you will develop the skills needed to become a level designer and gameplay programmer. Combine everything you have learned, from coding to design, to build a final prototype, in this in-depth, hands-on game development workshop. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

It is time to level up! Students will take what they previously learned and refine their game design skills. With a focus on polish, they will add extra content to their game, such as menus, visual effects, and multiple playable characters. The class will also tackle the most requested additions: custom character models and animations. This course requires previous game design knowledge and Unreal Engine experience. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students will jump into the world of computer science with Scratch, an age-appropriate programming language designed to teach the fundamentals of coding. They will explore graphics, animations, sound, and more as they design their own character and create an environment for it to live in. Students will then give their character a purpose by developing a storyline or gaming objective. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students will learn basic commands and functions, then continue building their projects using Python's advanced features. This course will help students become familiar with this popular and versatile language, whether they are new to coding or looking to enhance their skills. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students will learn everything from the basics of Maya modeling software through the process of fully realizing their creations. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

The video games of today owe much to how they were made decades ago. Using Unreal Engine, students will discover what it took to make a great game without realistic graphics and online multiplayer as they program their very own arcade video game. Pulling inspiration from classics like Pac-Man and Space Invaders, they will learn how to create a simple gameplay loop that never grows old. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students will learn more in-depth coding techniques to help them become productive and efficient programmers. Students will expand their programming skillset and gain the tools needed to write better code and achieve their goals. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Unleash creativity! Students will explore the exciting world of concept art, a key element in creating high-quality visuals for films, television shows, and video games. Whether it is a superhero showdown or an epic space vista, this course will teach students the fundamentals of making ideas visually stunning. They will create compelling stories, characters, and worlds that captivate audiences of all ages. The only limits are their imaginations. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

For musicians and non-musicians alike, this hands-on introductory course into music production uses the latest computer technology for creating, recording, and writing music. Learn the basics of music notation, audio and midi file types, mic types and placement strategies (hands-on work with mics, mixers, and interfaces), digital audio editing, Apple loops and beats, mixing (panning, reverbs and delays, submasters), software instruments and introduction to synthesis.

Students will also explore how to combine images, text, animations, and music to create unique clips that reflect their creativity. By the end of the week, students will have produced original media complete with sound and visual effects. All necessary equipment and cameras will be provided for classroom use. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

Java is an invaluable development platform used to create all kinds of computer applications, from Minecraft and Google Docs to Blu-ray players and Netflix. This entry-level course will teach students the various real-world uses of Java while they learn syntax, object-oriented programming, and other essential aspects of the programming language used by millions of software developers.

In the style of Mega Man, Mario, and Castlevania, students will have the chance to design their own classic side-scroller adventure. They will have complete control over the design of the video game and will create original characters and environments. Using Unreal Engine, tudents will design objects that can be picked up to help their avatar and create obstacles to increase the difficulty of the game. The course concludes with a prototype that can be further developed and shared with family and friends. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students who love drawing and animation will take their skills to the next level by using Maya modeling software to bring characters and designs into the 3D world. They will create their own 3D models in any style they choose, from cartoonish monsters to stylish race cars. Students will then add extra details that give their models personality and make them stand out. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Buckle up! Using Unreal Engine, students will learn the basics of creating a furiously fast racing game. They will tune their vehicle to their own liking and design a course filled with obstacles, ramps, speed boosts, and power-ups. Whether inspired by Forza or Mario Kart, students will leave with a playable prototype that can be taken home and further developed. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Experience a world through the eyes of a video game character! Students will learn the fundamentals of game design as they develop a first-person perspective game inspired by titles such as Call of Duty and Minecraft. Using Unreal Engine, they will build paths to follow, obstacles to avoid, and pick-ups to power up their character. By the end of the course, students will leave with a playable prototype that can be further developed and shared with family and friends. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students will run, jump, and play in a 3D adventure video game of their own creation. Whether they are inspired by classics like Super Mario 64 or modern hits like Fortnite, they will learn the game design fundamentals that make these games so engaging. Using Unreal Engine, students will design their own virtual world, set objectives, and explore everything they have built. The week concludes with a prototype that can be further developed and shared with others. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Whether inspired by Overcooked or New Super Mario Bros, cooperative play makes gaming more fun and challenging. This course will cover the many layers of co-op game design, from enemy interactions to the effects of friendly fire. Using Unreal Engine, students will create multiple controller inputs and build levels that require coordinated problem solving. Multiplayer video games introduce new challenges for players, but they also double the fun. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Ever since Minecraft, survival games have become a booming genre, with titles like Subnautica, ARK: Survival Evolved, and LEGO Fortnite leading the way. Using Unreal Engine, this course will guide students in creating their own landscape filled with harsh weather and dangerous enemies. By the end of the week, students will have developed the perfect gameplay loop of forage, craft, and survive. With the help of Utah Games graduates, students will ensure their game delivers the ultimate survival experience. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Who needs timers, points, or fail states? Popularized by Animal Crossing and The Sims, cozy games are all about soothing vibes and having a stress-free time, where you never lose. Using Unreal Engine, students will learn how to build inviting environments, design quests for cultivating friendships, and develop daily routines and rewards that make players feel right at home. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

From concepts, environments, and characters to visual effects and user interface, video games rely on a wide array of artists with diverse skills. Students will learn the ins and outs of video game artwork, including best practices and asset pipelines. Students will leave with a better understanding of their strengths and weaknesses and how these insights can help them discover a future profession. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Students who have chosen the programming side of game development will now get the chance to focus those skills. Students will learn the ins and outs of video game coding, including best practices such as commenting and debugging. Students will learn why problem solving is an essential part of a programmer's daily life and will leave with a better understanding of their strengths and weaknesses, helping them improve every line of code they write. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

Get your pulse racing with the martial art made famous by Jack Sparrow, Zorro, and even Yoda. Cut to the chase and learn the footwork, bladework, and etiquette of Olympic saber fencing. Discover defensive moves and how to trick your opponent by fencing with master teachers. Co-sponsored with Salt City Swords Fencing Club.

This summer, unleash your child's inner adventurer at our Scuba Explorers Camp! Perfect for young aquatic enthusiasts, this unique program offers a safe, fun, and educational introduction to the underwater world--all in a controlled pool environment. Campers will learn real scuba skills, build confidence, and discover a lifelong love for the ocean. Through SSI's Blue Oceans conservation program, kids will also explore marine life and learn how to protect our underwater ecosystems. While this is a recognition program (not a certification course), the skills gained will give your child a head start toward becoming an Open Water Diver in the future. All activities are supervised by certified SSI Explorers Instructors with a low participant-to-instructor ratio for maximum safety and personal attention. Co-sponsored with Neptune Divers.

Get ready for an unforgettable adventure and take the first step toward earning a lifelong scuba certification! Our 5-Day Scuba Camp introduces young divers to the exciting world of scuba through engaging classroom sessions and confined-water (pool) training. This camp is designed to build a strong foundation of knowledge and skills. After completing the five days, participants may continue their journey by enrolling with any SSI facility to complete their open water dives and earn their SSI Junior Open Water Diver certification. Co-Sponsored with Neptune Divers.

"Ride with Confidence! Discover the thrill of mountain biking in a fun and supportive environment! This Beginner Mountain Biking Camp is perfect for those new to the sport, focusing on building confidence, basic bike handling, and trail-riding skills. Under the guidance of experienced instructors, participants will learn proper braking, shifting, balance, and body positioning while navigating beginner-friendly trails. No experience? No problem! This camp is all about having fun, gaining new skills, and developing resilience as you explore the great outdoors on two wheels. BRING YOUR OWN BIKE Co-sponsored with Summit Journeys."

Take your mountain biking to the next level in this fun, challenging, and supportive Intermediate Mountain Biking Class. Designed for riders ready to progress beyond the basics, this class focuses on refining bike control, improving efficiency, and building confidence on more technical terrain. Riders will gain tools to move more smoothly and confidently on the trail while continuing to develop resilience and trail awareness.This camp is perfect for riders who already have foundational skills and are excited to challenge themselves, grow their confidence, and have fun exploring the outdoors on two wheels. In order to register, students must be confident riding on green trails, comfortable on uneven terrain including rocks, roots, and small obstacles, and have basic cornering skills on flat and moderately bermed turns. BRING YOUR OWN BIKE Co-sponsored with Summit Journeys

Club Pickleball USA will provide balls, paddles if needed, snacks and a whole lot of fun! The final day will feature a tournament format to showcase your new love of Pickleball! Co-Sponsored with Club Pickleball USA.

Unlock your child's potential through the dynamic world of Chinese martial arts! This engaging introductory program is specially designed for children and youth, offering them a foundation in Northern Shaolin Kung Fu. Participants will build confidence, improve focus, boost physical fitness, and gain essential self-defense skills. Beyond the physical benefits, students will explore key aspects of Chinese culture and values, making this a holistic learning experience. Every child will leave with skills that support lifelong personal growth. Co-Sponsored with Master Lu's Health Center.

Dive into adventure with our Intro to White Water Kayaking Camp! Designed for teens ready to explore the thrill of moving water, this camp combines hands-on skill building with personal growth and teamwork. Under the guidance of certified instructors, participants will learn kayaking fundamentals including paddle strokes, boat control, river reading, and safety techniques by starting in calm waters before progressing to beginner-level rapids. Along the way, campers will develop confidence, courage, and an appreciation for the power and beauty of rivers. This class will appeal to all learners. *The curriculum for Math Games Mania is similar in each section but slightly modified for the target age group.*

Participants will learn about solar, wind, and DC motors and discover the role machines play in everyday life. Using tools such as levers, cams, gears, and pulleys, students will build multiple models that simulate real-world machines like sweeping devices, windmills, and racing cars. They will also have the opportunity to create their own imaginative designs. Projects include solar cars, alien walkers, dog-bots, and more. By the end of the week, students will not only understand how these machines work but will also invent creative solutions of their own. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

This hands-on experience encourages creativity, problem-solving, and technical skills in a fun and engaging environment. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

This fun and exciting workshop will explain the systems of our body through the lens of childhood curiosity and play by talking about and exploring everything adults don't really want to talk about. Kids will spend the week learning things like how our body makes a scab, where ear wax comes from, why we hiccup, and what spit has to do with taste. Students will also make their own blood, brains, and snot! We are hoping that your kids will see the body in a whole new way and make lots of wonderful dinner conversation with you.

In one of our most popular workshops students will study the modern market system with a hands-on approach and engage in a mini-market game of risk, chance, and profit as they captain businesses of their own in the battle for market supremacy! They will learn the basic mechanics of the stock market and develop an understanding of market forces, trading techniques, and the fundamentals of analysis. Finally, students will learn how they fit into the economic world and the power of their own decisions in the interconnected world of commerce.

Students will have the opportunity to engage their curiosity about animals while investigating the outer and inner workings of animals like earthworms, grasshoppers, crawfish and frogs. Participants should be interested and willing to dissect, under supervision, multiple specimens; a strong stomach and curious mind is a must for this fun, hands-on dissection class!

Uncover the mysteries of mars! Throughout the week, discover what it takes to travel through and live in outer space. Show off your engineering skills by designing a rocket, building a landing device, and making a Mars robot to gather materials on the surface. You will even visit the Clark Planetariums Mars exhibit, where you will put the robots to the test! This is one mission you do not want to miss! Co-sponsored with the Department of Physics and Astronomy.

Calling all future engineers and space explorers! In this hands-on STEM camp, students will step into the role of rover engineers tasked with designing a machine to study Mars. Each day focuses on a new challenge -- from learning about Mars and its geology to building robotic arms, testing for water, and creating a motorized rover. Campers will explore coding with Microbits, experiment with hydraulics, and tackle real-world engineering problems like safe landings and mobility. The week wraps up with "Launch Day," where students test rockets and program their rovers to complete Mars-inspired tasks.

This class will teach the fundamentals of sports statistics as evaluators of efficiency and performance. We'll experiment with visualization techniques and learn how the implementation of stats has evolved over time. Class will culminate with competitive simulations to see who has what it takes to build the best data-driven team on a budget. (While primarily focusing on baseball, the class will touch on other pro sports as well).

This camp introduces students to the exciting world of robotics through Python programming. Designed for beginners, this course makes learning both coding and robotics approachable and engaging. Students will learn how to control sensors, motors, and real hardware as they bring their robot to life step by step. They will write code that enables their robot to navigate, respond to environmental changes, and complete fun challenges. Throughout the week, students will explore how logic, problem-solving, and creative design work together to build smarter and more capable behaviors. At the end of camp, each student will take home their robot, allowing them to continue experimenting and upgrading their creation beyond the classroom. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

This camp is designed for students ready to move beyond LEGO Mindstorms and explore advanced robotics concepts. Participants will work with a Bluetooth-enabled robot equipped with a 2.4GHz transmitter, ultrasonic transceiver module, dual light-level detector for line tracing, microcontroller, and Arduino boot loader--preloaded and ready to use. Students will tackle increasingly challenging obstacle courses and missions while learning new programming techniques through an intuitive drag-and-drop coding system. They will experiment with microcontrollers, sensors, and advanced robotics behaviors in a fun, hands-on environment. At the end of the week, students will take their robot home to continue learning and innovating. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

Let's get ready to rumble! This camp is perfect for students who enjoy hands-on engineering and friendly competition. Using LEGO Mindstorms robots, participants will design, build, and program custom robots to compete in Sumo-style battle rings. Students will learn how to protect microcontrollers and sensors through smart engineering and use creative design strategies to maximize their robot's performance. While the camp includes fun competitions, the focus is on learning, experimenting, and teamwork. By the end of the week, students will have developed technical skills and problem-solving abilities in a dynamic and engaging environment. Co-sponsored with Future Technology Education.

Have you ever wondered why some apps feel confusing, why certain chairs hurt your back, or why accidents happen even when people try their best? This camp introduces students to the science of human factors--the study of how people interact with technology, tools, and environments. Students will explore how our minds (attention, memory, decision-making) and bodies (size, strength, posture) influence design and usability. Through hands-on projects like setting up ergonomic furniture and analyzing real-world examples, students will learn how to create systems that enhance performance, improve safety, and increase user satisfaction. Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Launch into a week of cosmic discovery in this foundational astronomy camp. Young learners will explore the Sun, Moon, planets, stars, and asteroids while uncovering the scientific principles that make our solar system work. Using hands-on models, crater-making simulations, constellation-building activities, and guided experiments, campers will practice observing, questioning, predicting, and problem-solving. By combining structured learning with creative exploration, this camp nurtures curiosity and builds a strong conceptual understanding of the incredible universe above.

Why do we dream? Why do some things make us happy while others make us nervous? Why do we act differently around friends than family? In this camp, students will explore the fascinating world of psychology--the scientific study of the mind and behavior. Through engaging discussions and hands-on activities, students will learn how to ask smart questions about human behavior and gain valuable self-awareness and life skills. This is not about reading minds--it is about understanding what makes people think, feel, and act the way they do. Get ready to dive into one of life's greatest mysteries: the human mind! Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Does your student love true-crime stories and wonder what drives criminal behavior? This camp dives into the fascinating world of criminology and psychology. Students will explore the science behind why people commit crimes, review major theories and risk factors, and examine real-world applications of research. They will also learn about the psychological profile of psychopaths, including their emotions, relationships, and lifestyle, while discussing important ethical issues in the field. Through engaging discussions and activities, students will develop critical thinking skills and gain insight into human behavior. Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Make magic with your words this summer in the perfect course for the young writer. Learn special writing tricks such as how to create sparkling descriptions, memorable characters, and hooks that mystify your reader. Explore different writing genres like poetry and fiction, and find magical writing topics in everyday life. Borrow magic writing secrets from your favorite authors and even learn a real magic trick or two. In this playful course, students are encouraged to develop their writing confidence and 'abracadabra!' leave the week a proud author of your own children's book.

In this workshop, students will use the majority of the time to write, using various formats, writing prompts, and even adding to stories they are working on at home. They'll also share their work, thoughts, and positive feedback for other's work. We will incorporate individual as well as group exercises. Students will practice foundational skills, engage in creative and persuasive writing exercises, and stretch their boundaries in new ways to find and express their voice!

In this camp, students will learn how to write a play. This camp will teach students what makes a play, what makes a script, and is a way to expand their writing capabilities. Students should have a basic understanding of playwriting at the end of the week.

This week-long camp allows teens to immerse themselves in the wonderful world of journalism and media. Students will work both in the classroom and on the main campus improving their writing and critical thinking skills, conducting interviews, exploring careers in media and journalism, and beyond. Topics will include news writing, feature writing, sports writing, podcasting, and more. Pick your passion and we will work towards crafting a final piece at the end of the week!

If your student has any anxiety about college-level writing assignments under the scrutiny of AI detectors, then this class is for them. In a fun, relaxed environment students can grow their ability to craft an argument, do analytical research, and synthesize a composed message within an academic framework, all while focusing on topics that are actually interesting to them. Communication is one of life's most important skills; don't miss this chance to boost your students' confidence before heading off to school. This course is intended for students heading to college in the next two years. Co-Sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Join us for a fun week-long exploration of writing! This summer camp opportunity is a collaboration the University of Utah's Department of Writing and Rhetoric Studies and the Youth Education program. It is designed for high school students who are considering going to college and want to explore writing as a possible major or minor. Throughout the week, students will engage in a range of different activities relating to how writing builds worlds: our current world, imaginative worlds, and the world of the future. Workshops will focus on writing in a range of genres, including flash memoirs and poetry, crafting fictional characters and imaginary ecosystems, and scholarship essays. Each afternoon, we will spend time engaging in collaborative world-building through an extended role-playing game (RPG). Camp participants will have the opportunity to submit their writing to an anthology published by faculty and students in the Department of Writing and Rhetoric Studies. Co-sponsored with the Department of Writing and Rhetoric.

Turn imagination into art! Does your student have a story they are eager to share? In this camp, artist Steven Doran will guide students through the process of developing their own stories and transforming them into compelling visual narratives. Throughout the week, students will learn techniques to illustrate unique characters and concepts, bringing their ideas to life on paper or digitally. Students may choose to work traditionally or digitally. If working digitally, a personal laptop or tablet with digital art software installed is required. All traditional drawing supplies will be provided. Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Whether you're playing an RPG, dating sim, or an open-world action game, narrative game designers craft captivating stories and characters that pull you in and don't let go. In this course, students will explore the fundamentals of interactive storytelling, character development, and world-building. They will practice writing branching narratives, dialogue, and plotlines that keep players engaged and immersed. By the end of the week, students will have designed their own game concept complete with a compelling story arc. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

This verse-atile class will have your kid dropping couplets like they're hot! They will learn different poetry styles through both reading a variety of them and writing them by hand. This class will give them a taste of everything from Shakespeare to Langston Hughes to Nikita Gill. They will find their own poetic voice and be able to say, "I'm a poet, I want everyone to know it!"

Do you love sports and dream of a career in the biz? Join us for a week-long camp learning all about sports communications. We will travel onto the main campus to discover the University of Utah's top-notch Division I sports teams and facilities, all while learning opportunities for students interested in sports careers. Participants will also learn how to cover athletic teams and delve into the relationship between reporters, athletes, coaches, and beyond. We will examine careers in sports communications, try some hands-on sports broadcasting and journalism, and meet professionals in the field.

Get ready for an immersive writing experience led by an award-winning author! By the end of the week, students will have crafted a story that showcases their creativity and unique voice.

Writing takes a lot of practice and know-how. This class will bring your kid's ideas, creativity, and love of words together to help them craft a story. They will learn how to develop compelling plots and characters, how to hook an audience, and ways to weave memorable themes and captivating descriptions into the narrative. They will be writing by hand every day and learning what it takes to make writing part of their everyday life.

Learn to cook anything like a pro! Take your culinary skills to the next level and learn how to make your favorite everyday meals from scratch with confidence. By the end of the week, students will understand how fresh ingredients impact flavor and nutrition - and gain confidence to create balanced meals at home!

Mighty mages cast powerful spells and summon mythical creatures in this beautifully illustrated, elaborately designed, strategy card game. At its core, Magic is a strategy card game that pits one player's deck of cards against another player's deck. In deckbuilding, you will get to decide exactly what card combination of virtuous heroes, fearsome creatures, brave warriors, mystical lands and magical spells to include in your deck. You will learn the basics of deck-building as well as card-play strategies for different types of decks. Magic: the Gathering is a surprisingly deep, fast, fun and challenging game. After completing the camp, you will have multiple decks in your collection, plus extra cards to use as building blocks for future decks. This bootcamp is geared toward beginners. Co-sponsored with Game Night Games.

Board games have come a long way. Just as technology has advanced, so has board game design. This class covers a lot of ground in just a week by introducing students to major categories of "Euro" board games that have emerged in the "modern" era (2000-present), including cooperative, deck-building, tile placement, worker placement and social deduction games. Variety is the spice of fun when it comes to board games. A different category of game will be featured each day of week. In addition, each student will receive a copy of their favorite game played during the week. Co-sponsored with Game Night Games.

Looking for an amazing life skill, this is the class for you. This class will highlight food safety and sanitation, careers, introduce knife skills and cooking techniques, measurements and other basic culinary skills This is one of a few classes where you eat your class work!

Ready to take your cooking skills global? In this camp, we'll teach you all the essential knife skills, cooking terms, cooking ratios, and tips for preparing a variety of delicious meals from all over the world. No need to grab your passport as you will be prepared to start creating international masterpieces from the comfort of your own kitchen!

Our hearts beet for healthy foods! From breakfast to dinner, the foods we choose make a difference. With the notion, food is fuel this camp focuses on whole foods and starting from scratch. Whether it is homemade pizza dough or yogurt, you are sure to cook up delicious and nutritious meals. At the end of the week, you will put your new skills to the test in a friendly competition where you will whip up a tasty meal with a mystery ingredient. Win or lose - we are rooting for you! Co-Sponsored with the Department of Nutrition and Integrative Physiology.

Students will have the opportunity to recreate famous historical battles such as Bunker Hill (1775) , Monmouth (1778) and Guilford Courthouse. (1781) The course includes lots of historical background combined with board gaming fun - a truly revolutionary experience! Co-sponsored with Game Night Games.

Dungeons & Dragons has likely influenced every role-playing board game and video game you have ever played. Whether your character is a mighty paladin fighting a frost giant, or a clever rogue disabling an intricate trap, you'll become your character as you embark on an epic fantasy adventure together. The story may include everything from secret treasures guarded by flame-spouting dragons to feisty dwarves fending off hairy bugbears. Over five days, students will explore the fundamentals of running engaging games, from building immersive worlds and creating memorable characters to managing rules, pacing, and player dynamics. Through hands-on practice, improvisation challenges, and collaborative storytelling, students will gain the confidence and skills to design and run their own polished one-shot adventure or campaign opener by the end of the week.

Discover the art of game design without sitting in front of a screen! In this literal hands-on course, students will learn how to create engaging games using paper, dice, cards, and their own imagination. They will explore core design principles like mechanics, balance, and playtesting while building prototypes that bring their ideas to life. Co-sponsored with Utah Division of Games.

The art of the theater will come alive in this course as young actors will be learning theater skills and playing theater games. Discover the joy of performance through improv, radio theater, monologues and more while building acting skills, and participating in different theatrical activities. This flexible, engaging class offers a taste of many theatrical styles while building confidence, creativity, and collaboration. Co-Sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Expand your imagination, acting skills, and confidence in this engaging introduction to the world of theater! Whether your child is an experienced performer or brand new to the stage, this camp offers a fun and supportive environment to learn the essential tools every actor needs. Campers will explore storytelling, character development, and voice techniques while making new friends and discovering the joy of performance.

At the end of the week, you'll showcase your work in a special exhibit at the Museum! This experience will guide you as you dive into the creative process, develop your personal artistic voice, and stay true to your imagination. Co-sponsored with Utah Museum of Contemporary Art.

Make tons of tiny things! Miniature food, art, and an itty-bitty gallery. We'll use paint, foam clay, and a variety of materials while talking about scale and how to use it! We'll use instant photography to capture our miniatures. Each participant will curate their museum, display their art, and take home a completed scene in 1:12 scale. Co-sponsored with Utah Museum of Contemporary Art.

This camp combines fun and sustainable printmaking experimentation with a dose of art history, connecting students to the rich historical and contemporary roots of printmaking. They will also discover alternative applications for their prints, such as greeting cards, cloth patches, collages, artist books, and more! Co-sponsored with Utah Museum of Contemporary Art.

The day will be chock full of animal themed art using lots of colorful and creative materials. We'll dabble in painting, collage, mixed media, and foam clay sculpture. We'll have projects were campers get to choose their favorite animals too. At the end of the day, they'll have an artful zoo to take home! Co-sponsored with Utah Museum of Contemporary Art.

Welcome to the Art Cafe - Salt Lake City's most imaginative dining-inspired art studio experience! Designed exclusively for kids, this camp turns art-making into a deliciously fun adventure. Campers will "order" from a menu of creative projects, from painting and sculpting to mixed-media masterpieces. Just like at a real cafe, their "server" will deliver all the materials they need to bring their ideas to life. When the art feast is over, we will handle the cleanup so campers can savor every moment of creativity without the mess! Co-sponsored with Art Cafe SLC.

Introduce your teen to the beauty of Korean traditional ink painting (Sumukhwa) in this hands-on cultural art camp. Students will learn the techniques behind painting the "Four Gracious Plants" - plum tree, orchid, chrysanthemum, and bamboo - symbols of resilience and integrity in Korean culture. Along the way, they will explore brushwork, stamping, and the meaning behind these timeless designs. This camp is perfect for teens who love art, want to try something new, and enjoy learning about global traditions in a relaxing, creative environment.

This unique art camp blends creativity, storytelling, and Korean culture for an unforgettable experience! Students will design their own K-pop-inspired hero (or their quirky tiger sidekick "Derpy"), learn to write their name in Korean, and bring their character to life through multiple art projects. From painting and book-making to tote bag and T-shirt designs, students will explore different mediums while expressing their individuality. The week ends with a mini gallery show where campers proudly share their creations with family and friends.

This week-long arts camp invites students to explore creativity through hands-on making, experimentation, and play. Each day introduces a new project using mixed media materials like paper, cardboard, paint, and found objects in a supportive studio environment where creativity matters more than perfection. Projects range from stamp-making and sculptural paper vases to dream landscapes, mosaics, and expressive self-portraits. By the end of the week, students leave with multiple finished artworks, new skills, and a stronger sense of pride in what they can imagine and create. Each student will also have an opportunity to display one of their artworks in an exhibition at the Department of Art & Art History at the end of the summer. Co-Sponsored with the Department of Art & Art History.

Cosplay is the art of playing with clothing and props to represent characters from books, film, games, and more. If you love Halloween, science fiction or fantasy media, video games, or playing pretend, you'll find cosplay to be a fun and expressive activity. Cosplaying is open to everyone--all ages, abilities, body types, genders, and interest groups are welcome in the cosplay community! You don't need expensive tools or knowledge of sewing/crafting to be able to cosplay. Join us to learn the basics of cosplay design and creation and leave with your own, handmade cosplay prop and the knowledge you need to try out your own costume designs. Students will all work on the same type of cosplay prop, putting their own creative take on it.

View the world through a new lens in this photography boot camp! Spend the week taking an in-depth look at F/stops, shutter speed, ISO, and other digital camera functions and how to use them to your advantage. You will also learn composition, elements of design, lighting, and rule of thirds; so you can spend more time making great images and less time fixing them. But, that is not at all, try some experimental techniques along your digital photography journey.

Transform into a moving masterpiece in this one-week summer adventure! Inspired by the dazzling work of contemporary artists, young creators will craft their own spectacular masks and props, then bring them to life through dance and movement. Each day brings new discoveries as we blend visual arts with creative movement. Kids will design, build, and dance their way through a week of imagination and joy. The grand finale? A Friday showcase where our young artists perform in their own wearable art creations! Co-sponsored with Utah Museum of Contemporary Art & Ririe Woodbury Dance Company.

In this week-long camp, students will explore relationships between colors while building connections with one another. Through hands-on projects focused on pattern, color mixing, and material exploration, students will experiment with media such as tie-dye, bubble painting, and thread bracelet design. Students collaborate to share ideas, solve creative challenges, and create both individual and group artworks. Students will complete several projects to take home and will also create a collaborative artwork to be displayed in an exhibition at the Department of Art & Art History at the end of the summer.

Calling all young aspiring artists! Get ready for creativity, fun, and all things ceramics. Join us for an unforgettable journey, where you'll explore the mesmerizing technique of wheel-throwing, create hand built clay pieces, and be introduced to the magical world of glazing. No matter your age or skill level, unleash your creativity and explore the wonderful world of ceramics. Co-Sponsored with Salt Lake Pottery Studio.

In this hands-on art camp, students will use clay or other figures and learn how to reproduce them using professional mold-making and casting techniques. Campers will explore materials like silicone rubber, plaster, and ceramic slip, and practice creating molds that capture every detail of their designs. They'll then cast their figures in resin, plaster, or clay, gaining insight into the creative process used by artists and designers to make multiples of their work. This camp is perfect for students who love sculpting and want to take their skills to the next level!

In this hands-on art camp, students will explore the world of sculpting using air-dry and oven-bake clay. They'll learn techniques for building original characters and forms, working from visual reference in three dimensions, focusing on creativity and craftsmanship. By the end of the week, campers will have completed unique clay sculptures(which can serve as the foundation to use in the mold-making camp if they sign up for that too). This camp is perfect for young artists who love working with their hands and bringing their ideas to life!

In this beginner-friendly workshop, students will explore three fun and accessible printmaking techniques: cardboard cutout block printing, styrofoam block printing, and gelli plate printing. They'll learn how to design and create their own prints while experimenting with texture, color, and pattern. This class is perfect for young artists interested in learning multiple variations of printmaking.

This hands-on camp introduces kids to the vibrant world of glass art. Campers will explore the magic of glass fusion, creating unique, colorful projects throughout the week. From stringer plates to fabulous night lights, they will develop artistic skills and fall in love with the process of transforming glass into art. Co-sponsored with Reflective Art Studios.

This hands-on camp introduces kids to the vibrant world of glass art. Campers will explore the magic of glass fusion, creating unique, colorful projects throughout the week. From stringer plates to fabulous night lights, they will develop artistic skills and fall in love with the process of transforming glass into art. Co-sponsored with Reflective Art Studios.

This advanced linoleum block-printing camp guides students to learn the technical skills of relief carving and printing using linoleum blocks, gaining confidence with tools, safety, and multi-step printmaking processes. Students will experiment with inking and printing methods and explore the difference between raised vs. carved-away surfaces. By the end of the week, each student will have created their own custom-printed items!

From fine art and illustration to design and comic art, drawing is at the heart of it all. In this camp, students will learn how to manipulate ink using pens, brushes, and other unique techniques. They will practice shading and creating depth, add vibrant colors to make their artwork pop, and experiment with textures using a variety of mediums. This hands-on experience will help students develop confidence and creativity in their artistic skills. Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

This introductory drawing class starts with the basics and builds confidence step by step. Students will learn how to draw space using simple perspective, explore how people and animals are built, and turn shapes into exciting drawings. Along the way, young artists will practice observation, creativity, and problem-solving. Students will also have the opportunity to display one of their drawings in an exhibition at the Department of Art & Art History at the end of the summer. Co-Sponsored with the Department of Art & Art History.

In this introductory watercolor camp, students will explore the unique beauty of Utah through hands-on painting projects designed for beginners. Throughout the week, young artists will learn techniques for capturing the Wasatch Mountains, the red rock formations of Southern Utah, local wildflowers such as the sego lily, and native wildlife. Instructors will guide students through foundational watercolor skills, including brush control, color blending, layering, and creating texture. By the end of the week, each student will have a collection of Utah themed artwork that reflects both their growing skill and the natural world around them.

This class dives into drawing through the eyes (and hands!) of the masters. Students will explore how great artists solved drawing challenges, then try those ideas out in their own artwork. Students will experiment with mark making, play with different drawing materials, and practice sharpening their accuracy while building confidence and creativity. Each student will also have the opportunity to display one of their drawings in an exhibition at the Department of Art & Art History at the end of the summer. Co-Sponsored with the Department of Art & Art History.

In this introductory mixed media camp, students will explore multiple engaging art forms: watercolor, collage, scratchboard, and geli plate printing and more. Each day, the instructor will guide students through age appropriate projects that introduce new tools and techniques while encouraging creativity and experimentation. Students will learn how to combine paint, paper, ink, and texture to build layered artworks that express their own ideas and interests. By the end of the week, your child will bring home a mini portfolio of unique pieces and a stronger sense of confidence in their artistic abilities.

Hands, faces, heads, the human figure, all super hard to draw, right? In this class we cover all of those "hard to tackle" parts of... ourselves! Learn the methods to help simplify some of these challenging forms and then how to put them on paper. Together we will practice drawing gestures and basic anatomy. This is a great class for any young artist or aspiring character designer ready to challenge themselves and take their art to the next level.

Create your own custom skateboard in this creative and one of a kind painting class. Spend five days brainstorming, designing and creating your dream skateboard deck with custom wheels, trucks and of course artwork! Students will learn the ins and outs of designing an uniquely shaped illustration from concept to final. Come join this challenging class for creatives and skateboarding enthusiasts! Co-Sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

Calling all crochet enthusiasts, newbies, and wannabe yarn wizards! Get ready to unravel the secrets of the craft in this camp - your gateway to creating adorable granny squares, mastering pattern reading like a pro, and maybe even conjuring up some cute little plushies along the way. Say goodbye to tangled messes and hello to endless possibilities as you embark on your crochet adventure. Let's stitch it up, one loop at a time!

Visible mending makes each stitch a sign of who you are, where your clothes have been, and where they become unique, carrying a piece of you. In this course, we will explore different techniques for mending and embellishing garments via hand sewing.  Students will learn about the Japanese arts of Sashiko and Boro patchwork, as well as embroidery and applique.  Each student will be able to try all techniques and work on their own projects. Supplies will be provided, but students are welcome and encouraged to bring their own jeans (or other woven fabric garment) to mend or embellish. Co-sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

In this course, students explore how light, shadow, and environmental elements can be used as creative tools in artmaking. Through projects such as shadow-based works, cyanotypes, suncatchers, and a collaborative glass mural, students will experiment with new materials and processes while developing an understanding of how art can be interactive, site-responsive, and connected to everyday spaces. Emphasis is placed on exploration, collaboration, and translating environmental observation into visual form. Each student will also have an opportunity to display a selected artwork in an exhibition at the Department of Art & Art History at the end of the summer. Co-Sponsored with the Department of Art & Art History.

Students will work alongside local artist Nick Hubble and spend five days digging in deep with aerosol arts, exploring the ins-and-outs of spray paint techniques, murals, and street art. We will draw inspiration from the 'greats' of graffiti and street art - from the early days of 'rogue' artists like Basquiat to today's highly-collected urban art legends like Shepard Fairey and Banksy. Extra lab time will be provided for students to go hands-on with large spray paint mural projects and artworks of their own, as well as to hone in skills in stenciling, sticker or (slap) creations, lettering, and other street art essentials. Co-Sponsored with Higher Ground Learning.

From expressive characters to dynamic page layouts, Manga is a world rich with artistic tradition. In this camp, students will explore the history and evolution of Manga while learning how Japanese language and culture influence the art form. They will study a variety of Manga styles, practice professional drawing and inking techniques, and gain hands on experience with the tools artists use to bring stories to life. Throughout the week, students will design and illustrate their own Manga pages, developing both their artistic confidence and storytelling skills. This camp is perfect for fans of Anime and Manga who are excited to create their own original work.

Learn the tools and techniques that artists, writers, typists, and colorists use to make their comics for print, the web, and mobile devices. Aspiring artists will explore the comic book as a wholly developed narrative; commonly referred to as graphic novels, these works of art combine highly developed themes and visual art in one piece. Come ready to learn to create influencing stories, unique and interesting characters, mind-blowing worlds, and the imagination and passion to put it all together!

From expressive characters to dynamic page layouts, Manga is a world rich with artistic tradition. In this camp, students will explore the history and evolution of Manga while learning how Japanese language and culture influence the art form. They will study a variety of Manga styles, practice professional drawing and inking techniques, and gain hands on experience with the tools artists use to bring stories to life. Throughout the week, students will design and illustrate their own Manga pages, developing both their artistic confidence and storytelling skills. This camp is perfect for fans of Anime and Manga who are excited to create their own original work.

In this hands-on camp, students explore the full creative process of making a comic, from developing a story to creating finished illustrations. Using both industry-inspired and contemporary techniques, students will learn how artists plan, draw, ink, and color comics while developing their own visual style. Each student will complete a comic spread and receive a printed pamphlet featuring all students' work. Students will also have the opportunity to display their comic in an exhibition at the Department of Art & Art History at the end of the summer. Co-Sponsored with the Department of Art and Art History.

Take your cartooning imagination to the next level and let your goofy and wacky side free. Emphasis is placed on exploring imagination and will introduce young artists to drawing cartoons from different perspectives, both literally and figuratively! Young artists will be introduced to the simple design and extreme fun cartooning has to offer!

Enchantment! Fantasy! Art! In this camp, you will embark on a fantastical journey where creativity knows no bounds. From wand-making to creature masks, dragon eggs and potions, each day will unfold with new wonders waiting to be crafted! This camp is for budding artists, dreamers, and wizards in the making.

Young artists who love stories and adventure will enjoy this focused illustration camp. Throughout the week, students will design and complete their own fantasy map, moving step by step from rough sketches to a finished pen and ink illustration. They will practice linework and shading using both felt-tip and ink-dip pens, learn the basics of calligraphy to letter place names and legends, and discover image transferring and compositing techniques that help them layer landforms, borders, and decorative details into a cohesive design. By the end of the week, each student will have created a beautiful and complex work of art that could easily serve as a guide for Davy Jones or Bilbo Baggins.

This course introduces the foundations of interprofessional collaborative practice. Students will engage in self-directed learning with other disciplines through the exploration of values and ethics for interprofessional practice, roles and responsibilities of health care providers, interprofessional communication strategies, and the development of high functioning teams in health care. This course is designed to provide a framework for deliberately working together with other health professionals to maintain a climate of mutual respect and shared values in today’s complex health care environment, with the common goal of improving patient outcomes.

This course will introduce students to fundamental teaching skills and health professions pedagogy. Emphasis is on learning science and theory to inform the selection of education strategies. Approaches that support effective learning across varied educational settings and learner needs will be explored. Students will be encouraged to apply these theoretical underpinnings to their current practice.

course_name: AI at Work 1: Intro to AI
description: Discover how ChatGPT and generative AI are transforming professional work. This hands-on course introduces participants to the fundamentals of AI, effective prompt-writing strategies, and practical applications across office tasks, communication, and creative projects. Learners will explore text, image, and video generation, experiment with real-world use cases, and practice designing prompts that deliver clear, useful outputs. The course concludes with a focus on ethical considerations, responsible use, and strategies for building productivity with guardrails. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) understand how generative, agentic, and anthropic AI fit into the broader AI landscape; 2) write effective prompts using six core strategies (clarity, specificity, context, tone, creativity, personas); 3) apply ChatGPT to workplace tasks such as drafting emails, summarizing documents, and creating presentations; 4) generate and refine visual and video content with AI tools such as DALL·E; 5) identify high-value AI use cases within their industry and evaluate business benefits; and 6) recognize ethical risks--including bias, privacy, and hallucinations--and apply responsible AI practices in professional settings. This course uses OpenAI's ChatGPT as an instructional tool, with concepts transferable to other AI products.

Artificial Intelligence is evolving rapidly, but the core principles of working effectively with it remain steady. This intermediate, business-focused, hands-on workshop builds on the first course in our AI at Work Micro-credential and emphasizes Augmented Intelligence---using AI to enhance, not replace, human decision-making and productivity. The course will utilize the power of AI to assist in teaching and advancing the concepts covered. Participants will learn how to customize ChatGPT, apply advanced prompting techniques, explore multimodal (data analysis, images, charts, voice, browsing) and Custom GPT capabilities, and design AI-driven workflows that save time and boost results. Through guided practice, participants will create their own AI assistant or workflow prototype tailored to their role. Finally, learners will develop strategies for staying current as the AI landscape evolves, ensuring their skills remain relevant even as tools change. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) differentiate and position AI in the workplace, 2) master advanced prompting and customization, 3) design and apply AI-driven workflows, and 4) sustain and elevate AI practices. This course uses OpenAI's ChatGPT as an instructional tool, with concepts transferable to other AI products.

This advanced course-our third in the AI at Work Micro-credential-helps professionals build lasting, practical AI skills. Focused on business applications, this workshop goes further by emphasizing Augmented Intelligence (AuI): using AI to enhance, not replace, human expertise. Building on the first two courses in the AI at Work Micro-credential, this course equips participants to move beyond experimentation into responsible, measurable adoption. Participants will enter the course with a defined workflow and authentic work artifact, ensuring that learning activities are directly grounded in their real-world context. They will engage with industry-specific examples, test workflows in live labs, and address ethical and human-in-the-loop safeguards to keep AI trustworthy. Over six hours, participants will create and refine an AI-augmented workflow and produce a portfolio of six business-ready artifacts. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) identify and frame real-world opportunities for Augmented Intelligence (AuI), selecting workflows where AI can enhance human expertise while maintaining ethical oversight, 2) design and implement responsible AI workflows, including Prompt Playbooks, Guardrails Sheets, and Use-Case Canvases aligned with business goals and industry context; 3) measure and communicate the business value of AI adoption, developing dashboards and business cases that translate ROI into clear, executive-ready communication, 4) drive adoption and demonstrate applied mastery, creating change management strategies that overcome resistance, deliver quick wins, and showcase a portfolio of six business-ready artifacts. This course uses OpenAI's ChatGPT as an instructional tool, with concepts transferable to other AI products.

Strong project management skills help turn ideas into outcomes. This course introduces the essential concepts, language, and tools used to guide projects. You'll explore the full project lifecycle, from start to finish. It is designed for individuals new to project management or those seeking a clearer understanding or refresher. This course emphasizes high-level knowledge rather than tool-specific or methodology-based application. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) define core project management concepts and terminology; 2) describe the purpose and components of each phase in the project management lifecycle; 3) understand roles and responsibilities within a project team; 4) develop a basic project plan with clear objectives, timelines, and milestones.

Learn how to strengthen your project planning and execution with proven strategies and best practices. Through hands-on activities and real-world examples, you'll gain practical tools to guide complex projects to success. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) develop and implement effective project management plans; 2) optimize resource allocation and balance project priorities; 3) understand and avoid common project risks and pitfalls; 4) utilize KPIs, OKRs, and EVM to monitor project performance and drive continuous improvement.

As projects grow in complexity, mastering advanced Agile techniques becomes essential. This course builds on your foundational knowledge by exploring how to apply Agile across multiple teams, enhance collaboration, and improve sprint performance. You'll strengthen stakeholder engagement strategies, streamline backlog refinement, and use Agile metrics to support continuous improvement. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) apply strategies for scaling Agile in complex project environments; 2) improve backlog refinement and sprint planning for team effectiveness; 3) use Agile metrics and reporting.

Uncertainty is a part of every project and the ability to manage risk effectively can make the difference between success and failure. This course provides students with practical strategies for identifying and responding to project risks, along with an understanding of how risk management relates to both scope and resource management. You'll learn risk fundamentals, how to plan for and mitigate risk, how to communicate risk effectively to stakeholders, and the important ways risk management integrates will all elements of project planning. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) identify and categorize potential project risks; 2) develop structured risk management and communication plans; 3) implement stakeholder communication strategies for risk management; and 4) understand how risk management integrates with scope and resource management.

Strengthen your leadership skills and learn how to inspire high-performing teams by mastering strategies for team dynamics, conflict resolution, and clear communication. In this hands-on course, you'll explore a variety of leadership styles, practice negotiation techniques, and build executive presence through presentation exercises and role-play simulations. Walk away with practical tools to lead confidently and engage stakeholders for stronger project outcomes. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) develop leadership styles that enhance project team performance; 2) apply communication strategies to engage diverse stakeholder groups; 3) implement conflict resolution and negotiation techniques; 4) Strengthen emotional intelligence and active listening skills for better team dynamics.

Discover how to use AI to work smarter across every phase of your project. Learn to track performance in real time, automate reporting, and detect risks before they escalate. This course offers hands-on experience with AI-driven project management tools designed to streamline decision-making and boost outcomes. You'll also explore key ethical considerations around data use, bias, and transparency in AI-powered workflows, and stay ahead of the curve with an AI Trends Update that highlights the latest innovations shaping the future of project work. The learning objectives for this course include: 1) identify trends and risks in using AI for project management; 2) understand AI's application for project quality management; 3) use AI-powered tools to monitor project performance and automate project reporting; 4) implement AI-based evaluation frameworks to improve project closing processes.

Students will engage in clinical observation within community and hospital settings, while learning about the differences in pharmacy regulation and practice between Mexico and the United States.Pre-travel work includes a series of short, multimodal assignments to enhance Spanish language skills, review pharmacy practices, and explore cultural differences. This course is designed to broaden students' perspectives on global pharmacy practice while enhancing communication and cultural competency skills.

This clinical rotation is designed to provide students with exposure to the breadth of practice in the field of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (PM&R) from the management of acute musculoskeletal disorders to long-term follow-up of individuals with disabling conditions such as spinal cord injury and stroke. Students will work closely with attending physician faculty and resident physicians in both the inpatient and outpatient setting. Emphasis is placed on students gaining and understanding of the functional outcomes, and the team approach utilized in rehabilitation practice. Students will also have an opportunity to work with various allied health providers such as physical therapist to better understand the role of these individuals in the rehabilitation process. In addition, the student may elect to spend the rotation focused on a particular area of PM&R practice to obtain a more in-depth exposure to this particular area.

Emphasis is placed on obtaining a solid understanding of research methodology and research design strategies. Students will be expected to directly contribute to either an ongoing, collaborative research project or with the design and implementation of an independent research project. A variety of research topic areas are available depending on faculty availability. These potential topic areas include, but are not limited to, spinal cord injury, traumatic brain injury, stroke, amputee rehabilitation, musculoskeletal rehabilitation, electrodiagnosis, and sports medicine.

This course will provide students with a working knowledge of the U.S. food system, food and nutrition policies and programs, and community nutrition program development. Students will use evidence-based nutrition epidemiology research to equip themselves to address critical issues in public health nutrition, such as: 1) the ways social, behavioral, food and nutrition factors influence the health of populations, 2) how nutrition and food policies influence health in vulnerable populations, and how to design programs to improve the nutritional status of a population. Special emphasis will be placed on nutrition programs and policies for maternal and child health, and chronic disease prevention.

The purpose of the course is to provide students with an overview of some key issues in the field of reproductive health and help them develop the conceptual skills to identify and evaluate how health services delivery, social, cultural, and policy issues impact and are impacted by health issues.

This course is structured under the organizing practice model of PEO and incorporates the Biomechanical/Rehabilitative and COOP models in order to frame assessment, treatment, and evidence-based practice for clients with neuromuscular disorders and spinal cord injury. Students will learn to interview and assess a client’s occupational profile, select appropriate outcome measures, plan and implement treatment, and evaluate evidence related to best practices for clients. Interventions will include energy conservation/work simplification/joint protection/pacing, ADL Adaptations, transfers/bed mobility, home exercise programs, managing lines, dysphagia, and home safety evaluations. Clinical reasoning, occupation-based practice, and client-centered care will be taught and threaded through course activities and assignments.

The purpose of this course is to introduce mathematical concepts and statistical methods used in modern engineering analysis. The goal is to introduce students to analytical and numerical tools that can be used to solve real world engineering problems. Lectures will be supplemented by several programming exercises using R and/or Matlab, and a large number of practical examples on relevant engineering topics. This course covers the role of statistics in engineering, probability theory and distributions, continuous random variables, random sampling, data description, and statistical analyses or a single sample, and common hypothesis testing.

The course introduces a wide range of standard mechanical elements that are extensively used in today's engineering world. The topics include reliability, fits and tolerances, rolling element and fluid film bearings, fasteners, welded joints, shafts, and material selection.

This course focuses on the modeling, analysis and control of dynamic systems. The modeling portion of the course includes mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, thermal, and fluidic systems. Methods employed involve solving sets of coupled differential equations using time-domain (i.e., state-space), frequency-domain (i.e., Laplace transform), and numerical techniques. The control-systems portion of the course focuses on the use frequency-domain techniques, and includes topics such as block diagrams, stability analysis, steady-state error, PID control, and root-locus design.

The communication emphasis is on delivering information in a clear, concise and easily consumable fashion. Students will learn to produce different types of technical communications, tailor messages to different audiences, provide peer reviews and work collaboratively. Critical thinking, teamwork, ethical considerations and organizational issues of engineering organizations will also be addressed.

Through a series of hands-on exercises and interactive presentations from practicing laboratory professionals, this course serves as an introduction to the Medical Laboratory Sciences profession and curriculum.

This course provides an introduction to the principles of human genetics with emphasis on human examples and applications. It covers classical genetics including the rules of inheritance, transmission genetics and genes in population. It also includes the molecular basis of gene structure, function, expression, and evolution.
Introduction to nucleic acid isolation, amplification, and detection techniques used in infectious disease, genetic, and oncology testing in the clinical laboratory.

Students work under the guidance of a faculty mentor to explore an in-depth topic in medical laboratory science and engage in honors research.

In the first section of the course, basic principles of research will be covered including how to identify research topics, evaluate the literature, construct and test a working hypothesis, analyze and interpret data, and report results. Basic research terminology and major formats of research designs will be discussed. In the second section, students will learn about basic principles of education including writing and evaluating learning objectives and examination items as well as teaching techniques especially those relevant to the medical laboratory, Topics related to accreditation, certification, and licensing in medical laboratory science will also be discussed.

The study of laboratory management and supervision, including organizational principles, financial management of essential resources, human resource management and leadership theory. Didactic coursework and assignments focus on development of effective teamwork, written and oral communication skills, critical evaluation of management-related case studies, compliance and regulatory issues, cultural competency, and ethical decision-making.

Clinical experience in pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical testing of blood and other body fluids for their biochemical components (e.g. blood gases, hormones, vitamins, therapeutic drugs, trace elements, toxins) using modern analytical techniques (e.g., electrophoresis, immunochemistry, chromatography, spectroscopy, mass spectrometry).

Clinical experience performing routine analysis of blood and other body fluids for their biochemical components (e.g., electrolytes, enzymes, hormones, lipids, non-protein nitrogen compounds, proteins) using automated and manual procedures. Students will participate in pre-analytical, analytical, and post-analytical phases of testing.

Clinical experience performing tests to establish a diagnosis, detect unsuspected diseases, or monitor effects of various treatment protocols for anemias, leukemias, lymphomas, and other hematologic disorders. Also includes experience in body fluid evaluation and urinalysis.

Includes experience in a special hematology laboratory performing tests designed to aid in the differential diagnosis of leukemias, lymphomas and other hematologic malignancies. Also includes rotations in the immunologic and hematologic flow cytometry laboratories.

Evaluation of normal hemostasis, hemostatic disorders, the associated clinical symptoms, and the laboratory testing necessary for diagnosis. Includes laboratory practice in the performance of diagnostic tests.

Practical application of Immunohematology principles including collection and processing of blood, component therapy, evaluation of prenatal and perinatal blood specimens, pretransfusion compatibility testing, transfusion reaction evaluations and quality assurance. Serologic testing and problem-solving skills such as antibody identification are emphasized.
Isolating and identifying commonly encountered pathogenic bacteria from clinical specimens.
Isolation and identification of yeasts, molds, and parasites in the clinical laboratory, using classical identification methods, rapid methodologies, and instrumentation.
The integration of the theory and practice of immunology in a clinical setting including immunologic assays used in the diagnosis of infectious disease, autoimmune disorders, and immune deficiencies.
Nucleic acid isolation, identification and amplification techniques used in disease diagnosis in the clinical laboratory.
